title: EU embargo on seaborne Russian crude and G7 price cap of 60 dollars per barrel take effect
body:
On 5 December 2022, the European Union's embargo on seaborne imports of Russian crude oil took effect together with a price cap of 60 US dollars per barrel on Russian crude. EU member states had agreed the cap on 2 December, following an agreement among the G7 states, and Australia also joined. A ban on imports of petroleum products was scheduled for 5 February 2023.

Under the mechanism, services linked to shipping Russian oil, including transport, brokering, financing and technical assistance, are restricted, but oil sold at or below the cap is exempt from part of those restrictions. The cap was to sit at least 5 percent below average market prices, using International Energy Agency data, with the first review due by mid-January 2023 and further reviews every two months. Cargoes bought and loaded before 5 December and arriving before 19 January 2023 had a 45-day transition period, and transports after a change to the cap had 90 days.

The Centre for Eastern Studies noted that member states disagreed on the level. Poland and the Baltic states wanted about 30 dollars, while Greece, Cyprus and Malta wanted 70 dollars or more. Pipeline oil was outside the price limits. Urals crude sold at European ports for roughly 48 to 58 dollars per barrel, below the cap.
